title: Automated triage-card enrichment and live-handoff telemetry capture
author: Avery K. Nguyen
description:
Motivation:
We observed frequent noisy handoffs where the on-call engineer lacked a compact, privacy-safe telemetry snapshot at assignment time. That leads to context churn and slow escalations. This PR adds an opt-in enrichment pipeline that captures a lightweight, redacted telemetry bundle at triage assignment and attaches it to the incident-bot handoff card. The goal is to improve mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for first responders and reduce chase-back requests for logs and traces.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new 'handoff-card' enrichment flow that runs when a triage card is created or reassigned.
- Captures a minimal telemetry snapshot: top-3 relevant logs, a 1s top-span trace summary, recent error-rate deltas, and a small metric rollup. Payload size capped and redacted by default.
- Implements configurable retention TTL and opt-in policy per team (feature flag + team-level annotation).
- Exposes a CLI flag to trigger manual snapshot refresh for a card (incident-bot snapshot refresh).
- Adds observability: metrics for enrichment success/failure, snapshot size histogram, and a handoff-quality signal (hand_off_with_snapshot / handoff_total).
- Adds unit and integration tests + an e2e harness run in CI that exercises the enrichment flow against the test telemetry sandbox.

Design notes and safety: 
- Privacy: snapshots are passed through the existing sanitizer pipeline. The sanitizer now applies an additional TTL-based redaction for attachments that contain stacktraces or PII-like tokens. Teams can opt out via a team annotation.
- Performance: enrichment runs asynchronously with bounded concurrency; worker pool size defaults to 4. We added backpressure logic to avoid amplification of alert storms (cards older than 5 minutes skip enrichment when system load > 80%).
- Fail-open: if enrichment fails, the handoff card still posts; failures are recorded in metrics and retried with exponential backoff.

Files changed (high level):
- cmd/incident-bot/main.go: add CLI switch --refresh-snapshot and feature-flag wiring.
- service/handoff/enricher.go: new module implementing capture + sanitize + attach.
- service/handoff/worker_pool.go: bounded async worker implementation and backpressure heuristics.
- web/ui/handoff_card.tsx: UI for showing snapshot summary with 'view details' and 'request-redaction' actions.
- infra/feature_flags.yaml: new flag triage.snapshot_enrichment (default: false).
- telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics and dashboards definitions.
- tests/integration/handoff_enrichment_test.go: integration harness against telemetry sandbox.
- docs/handbook/handoff_enrichment.md: operational runbook for teams to opt-in/out.

Commits (summary):
- 2f9b2c9 feature: initial enricher scaffolding and worker pool
- 7a0d1f3 sanitizer: add TTL redaction rule and safer token regex
- c44b3a1 ui: display compact snapshot and add manual-refresh button
- 9d3e8a7 ci: integration harness and retry tests
- e6f12b0 docs: handbook entry and runbook

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests covering sanitizer logic and worker backpressure.
- Integration test spins up the telemetry sandbox (mock traces/logs) and asserts that snapshots are attached and redacted.
- CI initially failed on a flaky test (TestHandoffEnrichment_Retries) due to timing; increased timeouts and added deterministic retry backoff in test harness. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, e2e mock).

Review conversation (abridged):
- Maya Patel: "Love the safety-first approach. Please call out the retention policy UI surface and make sure the default is conservative."
- Author (Avery): "Added docs and enforced conservative defaults (flag off, TTL=24h). Updated UI to show TTL and opt-out button."
- Jonas Schneider: "Concern about worker pool sizing; can we expose the pool size as a cluster config?"
- Author: "Exposed via ENV/helm value 'HANDOFF_ENRICHER_WORKERS' with sane default 4; documented in helm chart."
- Priya Reddy: "Can we add alerting if enrichment success rate < 90%?"
- Author: "Added alert rule telemetry.alerts.handoff_enrichment_fail_rate > 0.1 for 5m with team owner tags."

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature is gated behind triage.snapshot_enrichment flag. We will start with opt-in for the SRE onboarding team (ENG-6041) and run a 2-week trial. After stability verification, we will flip the default to on for internal teams only. Public customers must explicitly enable the feature in their private deployment config.

Release notes (short):
- incident-bot: add optional triage-card telemetry snapshots to improve handoffs; guarded by feature flag triage.snapshot_enrichment. Includes UI, CLI, and observability.

Operational runbook summary (docs/handbook/handoff_enrichment.md):
- How to enable/disable per team
- How to request redaction and manual snapshot refresh
- Troubleshooting enrichment failures (inspect enrichment-worker logs, check sanitizer traces, look up snapshot metrics)

Security review:
- Security reviewed sanitizer changes to ensure redaction rules don’t leak secrets. Security requested an additional regex audit which was completed and committed in commit 7a0d1f3.

Performance notes:
- At default concurrency, enrichment adds <120ms median extra latency to card creation (async path), with tail bounded by external telemetry calls. Backpressure prevents amplification during alert storms.

Why this is different from existing runbook/enrichment features:
- Focus on a tiny, high-signal snapshot that is privacy-aware and TTL-managed rather than full incident dumps. Designed specifically to reduce initial context-churn for first responders.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers (Maya, Jonas, Priya). CI green after retries. Merged via squash to main on 2025-08-20.

Notes for follow-ups (todo):
- ENG-6041: measure MTTA delta after opt-in trial (metric instrumentation done).
- Add RBAC gating so only certain roles can request raw snapshot exports (follow-up PR).
- Explore embedding-based snapshot summarization to reduce size (research spike).
